title: Where do you choose which account the hub's agents run on?
lead: Should the hub get an Account card where you see which account the agents use and switch between a plan sign-in and an API key, with the key kept in Windows' protected storage? I recommend it: switching today means environment variables and a terminal sign-in.
for_you: Click the usage meters to open the Account card: it shows the account in use and lets you switch, with a Cancel exit
Switching restarts the hub, and running agents stop their turn and carry on afterwards

for_you.text: A pasted API key is kept in Windows' protected storage for your user, never in a project folder or the repo
Switching the plan sign-in also switches Claude Code for your other sessions on this PC until you switch back

context: Matt (2026-11-17) is testing how the hub works on another plan for a colleague. Today agents use the PC's Claude Code sign-in; with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus CRUX_HUB_USE_API_KEY=1 set before start they use an API key instead (hub/README.md, lib/agent.mjs; the API-key start has not been tested end to end). Usage shows as plan meters in the strip (decision 36), which only exist for a plan sign-in. Per-project settings live on a card opened from each project's level chip (decision 44). A plan sign-in is meant for its owner; a colleague is best tested on their own machine or Windows user, or with an API key.

options.name: Account card, one account for the hub
options.summary: An Account card opened from the usage meters: shows the account in use, chooses Plan sign-in (with Sign in as someone else) or API key (paste field), kept in Windows' protected storage; Switch restarts the hub. Plan meters for a plan; tokens and dollars for a key.
pros: No terminal or environment variables; you always see which account is billing
Key never sits in a file in a project or the repo
cons: One account for all projects at a time
A plan switch also changes your other Claude Code sessions on this PC

options.name: A, plus an account per project
options.summary: As A, and each project's card can use a different API key, with a badge on its thread when it differs from the hub's.
pros: A colleague's or client's work can bill to its own key
cons: More to build and test; usage and budgets split by key

options.name: Show the account only
options.summary: The usage panel says which account is active and links to how to switch outside the app.
pros: Smallest; nothing new holds a key

recommendation: A: one Account card for the hub, key in Windows' protected storage. Per-project keys (B) can come later if a project really needs its own bill.
change_mind: If a project must bill to someone else's key while others run on yours, take B.

settles.value: chosen in the hub's UI (plan sign-in or API key), one account for the hub; API key kept in the OS's per-user protected storage, never in a project or repo; switching restarts the hub
